findings.title: JWT Verification Bypass - Unverified Token Decoding
findings.impact: Complete authentication bypass allowing attackers to forge JWT tokens and impersonate any user, accessing all protected endpoints and user data without valid credentials
findings.evidence: Function currentUser() uses jwt.decode() instead of jwt.verify(). The decode function only parses JWT content without validating the signature, allowing any attacker to create a valid-looking token claiming to be any user with any role. Same issue on line 12 in tagRequest().
findings.recommendation: Replace jwt.decode() with jwt.verify() using a secret key: const claims = jwt.verify(bearer, process.env.JWT_SECRET). Ensure JWT_SECRET is stored securely in environment variables. Add proper error handling for invalid tokens.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Invoice Query - Unparameterized ORDER BY Clause
findings.impact: Allows arbitrary SQL injection through the order parameter, enabling time-based data exfiltration, table modification/deletion, and potential full database compromise via blind SQL injection techniques
findings.evidence: The GET /invoices endpoint constructs SQL with direct string interpolation: SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE owner_id = $1 ORDER BY ${order} where order comes from req.query.order without validation. An attacker can inject SQL after ORDER BY, such as: ?order=created_at;DROP TABLE invoices;-- or use CASE statements for blind injection.
findings.recommendation: Implement whitelist validation using an enumeration object: const SORTABLE = { created_at: 'created_at', amount: 'total_cents', status: 'status' }; const order = SORTABLE[req.query.order] || 'created_at'. This ensures only safe column names are used.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) - Unvalidated URL Fetching
findings.impact: Allows attackers to make the server perform HTTP requests to arbitrary URLs including internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), and internal APIs, leading to information disclosure and potential credential theft from cloud environments
findings.evidence: The fetchLogo() function accepts any URL parameter and passes it directly to fetch(url, { redirect: 'follow' }). No hostname whitelist is applied (unlike fetchAsset() which has one). This is called from POST /branding/preview endpoint with user-controlled req.body.logoUrl. Attackers can request http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data or http://localhost:6379 to access sensitive services.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL validation with whitelist: Add const ALLOWED_HOSTS = new Set(['assets.example.com']); Check hostname against whitelist before fetching. Change redirect option to 'error' to prevent redirect-based attacks. Validate Content-Type header to ensure only images are returned.
